headline: Approved riprap repairs to Hamden Hills Drive Bridge footings and, 5-1, sediment and brush removal at Pardee Brook Diversion Channel, 2623 Dixwell Avenue.
summary: Members approved a Town plan to stabilize the footings of the Hamden Hills Drive Bridge over Shepard Brook, with conditions. They also approved, 5-1, removing sediment and brush from the Pardee Brook Diversion Channel. Minutes of the September 2, 2026 meeting were approved as written.
decisions: Approved the Town's application to stabilize the Hamden Hills Drive Bridge footings over Shepard Brook, with conditions, by unanimous vote.
Approved the Town's application for sediment and brush removal at the Pardee Brook Diversion Channel, with conditions, by a 5-1 vote.
Approved the minutes of the September 2, 2026 regular meeting as written.

decision_evidence.quote: All voting members were in favor of approving IWC #26-1275. The application was approved with conditions as recommended by Mr. Vocelli and revised by the Commission, as follow:

Commissioners McCollum, Stone, Schneider, Shadle, and Laliberte voted in favor of approving IWC #26-1276; Commissioner Hayes voted against. The application was approved subject to the conditions recommended by Mr. Vocelli.
Commissioner Schneider moved to approve the minutes as written. Commissioner McCollum seconded the motion. All members voted in favor; the September 2, 2026, meeting minutes were approved as written.

decision_titles: Stabilization of Hamden Hills Drive Bridge footings over Shepard Brook
Maintenance of Pardee Brook Diversion Channel, 2623 Dixwell Avenue
plain_text:
Page 1 of 8 Inland Wetlands Commission 10.7.26 Minutes 
 
Town of Hamden 
Planning and Zoning Department 
 
Inland Wetlands Commission 
Meeting Minutes 
 
Hamden Government Center 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel: (203) 287-7070 
Fax: (203) 287-7075 
 
October 14, 2026 
The Inland Wetlands Commission, Town of Hamden, held a hybrid Regular Meeting on 
Wednesday, October 7, 2026. The meeting was held in-person in the Legislative Council Chambers 
at Hamden Memorial Town Hall, 2372 Whitney Avenue, Hamden, CT 06518, and remotely via 
Town Zoom teleconferencing at https://hamden.zoom.us/j/82474089466.  
 
Commissioners in Attendance: 
 
In Person: Michael Milazzo (Chairman), David McCollum (Vice 
Chairman), Michael Stone, Kirk Shadle, George 
Schneider, Elizabeth Hayes, Deb Laliberte 
  Staff in Attendance: In Person: Eugene Livshits (Town Planner), Thomas V ocelli, 
(Wetlands Agent), Maisie Albis (Commission Clerk) 
Via Zoom: Tim Lee (Assistant Town Attorney) 
  
Chairman Milazzo called the meeting to order at 7:01p.m. Commissioner McCollum called the 
roll and established a quorum.  
 
A. Public Comment Session 
 Chairman Milazzo invited comments from the public. An in-person attendee, Marc Vece, 
approached the podium to speak. He identified himself as the president of the Meadowbrook Third 
Co-Op and spoke to concerns the group has regarding Pardee Brook and the diversion channel 
maintenance proposed by IWC #26-1276. Mr. Vece reported that water flow is heavily restricted by 
sediment. As a result, he said that residents often need to contact Public Works to activate a pump 
system after storm events in order to manage flooding. Mr. Vece concluded with a request that the 
Commission do what it can to help the community resolve the ongoing issue. 
No other in-person attendees made comments. The Chairman confirmed with the clerk that there 
were no online attendees who wished to speak, then closed the public comment session. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
B. Application Review 
 1. IWC #26-1275 Received 09/02/2026 
Hamden Hills Drive Bridge over Shepard Brook 
Stabilization of bridge footings 
Applicant: Town of Hamden 
Town Engineer Stephen White and Assistant Town Engineer Jose Alvarez presented the 
application. Mr. Alvarez joined the meeting remotely, sharing his screen to show the proposed
Page 2 of 8 Inland Wetlands Commission 10.7.26 Minutes 
 
plans. Mr. White stated that erosion has exposed the foundation of the bridge and protective 
measures must be taken to stabilize the structure. Multiple options were considered, he said, but 
the ultimate proposal is to install riprap around the bridge columns to rebury the exposed 
footings. 
Mr. Alvarez explained that the State inspects bridges on a regular basis and recently increased 
the frequency of inspections for the Hamden Hills Drive Bridge due to scour. The CT Department 
of Transportation has notified the Town that the bridge requires repair, Mr. White added. The 
current proposal was designed in response to that notification. 
Mr. White stated that 12”-18” intermediate riprap would be used, and that Public Works 
would be assisting with the repair work. Mr. Alvarez noted that work extended into the wetland 
area but not into the waterway itself. At the conclusion of their presentation, Chairman Milazzo 
called for questions from the Commission.  
Commissioner Shadle remarked on the undercutting he noticed on the channel bank. Mr. 
White confirmed that work would be focused on the eroded western bank. Commissioner Shadle 
then asked whether the intention was to restore the channel to its original design conditions or to 
reinforce the existing conditions. Mr. White confirmed it was the latter. He noted that, though the 
objective was not to restore the original conditions, the proposed riprap slope would approximate 
the original stream bed.  
In response to another question from Commissioner Shadle, Mr. White said that the riprap 
would extend upstream roughly 12 feet  from the end of the foundation. He clarified an earlier 
statement by Mr. Alvarez regarding work taking place in the waterway: the riprap would extend 
over the existing northwest bank, thus into the stream, but would end near the original bank.  
Mr. White said that no work was planned for the northeast bank at this time. Mr. Alvarez 
explained that the current proposal for the northwest bank addressed an immediate necessity to 
prevent the loss of capacity of the bridge; a separate application would be filed if future 
evaluations demonstrate that work is needed on the other bank.  
Commissioner Schneider raised concerns about potential downstream erosion. He reported 
that some disturbance to the far bank was observed during the site walk. He wondered whether 
the narrowing of the stream could increase the flow velocity and worsen the disturbance. Mr. 
White acknowledged the possibility that the work might increase flow, and indicated that bank 
stabilization could be considered if warranted.  
Commissioner McCollum had several questions. He first asked whether the site plan 
indicated how construction equipment would enter the site. Mr. White did not believe the plans 
showed the access point, but recalled it to be from a parking lot off of Shepard Avenue to the 
north of the work site. Commissioner McCollum asked about the feasibility of doing the work 
from the Farmington Canal Trail. Mr. White said that the goal was to do as much work from the 
trail as possible, though some equipment may need to be brought further down the embankment.
Page 3 of 8 Inland Wetlands Commission 10.7.26 Minutes 
 
At Commissioner McCollum’s request, Mr. Alvarez pointed out the potential access points at the 
north and south of the work site on the plan. 
Commissioner McCollum then asked when the work was anticipated to occur and what the 
timeline for completion might be. Mr. White replied that the timing was somewhat dependent on 
the availability of Public Works staff but ideally work would begin in late October or November. 
Mr. Alvarez added that weather was also a factor, as work will need to take place during a dry 
season.  
Mr. White and Mr. Alvarez responded to a number of questions from Commissioner 
McCollum to say that: equipment was not anticipated to be stored on-site but could be kept on the 
shoulder of the trail if necessary; no similar maintenance has been performed on the bridge 
footings, though riprap was added to the embankment slope at some point; the estimated design 
service life for the bridge is around 75 years and the repairs are intended to last the duration of 
that lifespan; dewatering will not be necessary. 
Noting that the application also presented alternative approaches, Commissioner McCollum 
asked what the determining factor would be in finalizing the plan. Mr. White replied that cost 
considerations resulted in a preference for the riprap approach. He added that the more 
challenging gabion basket alternative could create additional disturbance as equipment may need 
to be brought further down the bank. He said that he was willing to reconsider the alternative 
approach if the Commission wished.  
Commissioner Schneider asked whether the riprap technique was a traditional method of 
minimizing scour under abutments, which Mr. White confirmed. There were no further questions 
from the Commission.  
Chairman Milazzo remarked that the member who makes a motion to approve the application 
should also read the suggested conditions offered by Mr. V ocelli. Commissioner Schneider 
made the motion and requested that Mr. Vocelli read those conditions into the record. 
Commissioner Shadle seconded. The suggested conditions were as follow: 
1. Access routes to the work site shall be limited to Town property and/or to public rights-of-
way. If any encroachment onto private property proves to be necessary, prior written consent 
from the owners shall be required;  
2. Heavy equipment shall remain on hard pavement or on upland soil; 
3. A downstream turbidity curtain and oil containment boom shall be installed prior to the onset 
of work in the watercourse; 
4. Rip rap stone shall be washed before installation; 
5. The stabilization project shall be scheduled for a dry weather period, but any inspection or 
maintenance schedules mandated by the State shall take priority;
Page 4 of 8 Inland Wetlands Commission 10.7.26 Minutes 
 
6. The October 2, 2026 Regional Water Authority comment letter shall be included on the final 
revised plans. RWA recommendations shall be considered binding conditions-of-approval, 
subject to any modifications herein;  
7. The applicant's final revised plans shall be signed and sealed by a professional engineer;  
8. The Notice-of Decision to be issued by the Wetlands Agent shall be included on the final 
revised plans, and all conditions-of-approval shall be listed and incorporated into those plans. 
The final revised plans shall be subject to review and approval by the Wetlands Agent or by 
the Chair of the Commission;  
9. Either repair alternative depicted by the applicant on the submitted plan is acceptable. Prior to 
the onset of the project the applicant shall confirm in writing which option has been chosen 
and the reason(s) for the choice. 
Commissioner Shadle raised the idea of a condition requiring a post-construction inspection. 
He and other members discussed the State’s authority with respect to bridges. Ultimately it was 
decided that such a condition would not be necessary. 
Commissioner McCollum recommended that additional language in Condition 2 should 
require that any temporary access routes needed to gain further access to the site are indicated on 
the plans. Commissioner Schneider suggested amending Condition 1 instead, and suggested that 
all access routes be depicted. Members also agreed that there should be language requiring that 
areas of disturbance be restored. Commissioner Schneider offered the following revision:  
1. Access routes to the work site shall be limited to Town property and/or to public rights-of-
way, and shall be depicted on the final revised plans. If any encroachment onto private 
property proves to be necessary, prior written consent from the owners shall be required. Any 
disturbance shall be stabilized and reseeded as necessary. 
Both Commissioner Schneider and Commissioner Shadle accepted the change, and Chairman 
Milazzo called for a vote. All voting members were in favor of approving IWC #26-1275. The 
application was approved with conditions as recommended by Mr. Vocelli and revised by 
the Commission, as follow: 
1. Access routes to the work site shall be limited to Town property and/or to public rights-of-
way, and shall be depicted on the final revised plans. If any encroachment onto private 
property proves to be necessary, prior written consent from the owners shall be required. Any 
disturbance shall be stabilized and reseeded as necessary. 
2. Heavy equipment shall remain on hard pavement or on upland soil; 
3. A downstream turbidity curtain and oil containment boom shall be installed prior to the onset 
of work in the watercourse; 
4. Rip rap stone shall be washed before installation; 
5. The stabilization project shall be scheduled for a dry weather period, but any inspection or 
maintenance schedules mandated by the State shall take priority;
Page 5 of 8 Inland Wetlands Commission 10.7.26 Minutes 
 
6. The October 2, 2026 Regional Water Authority comment letter shall be included on the final 
revised plans. RWA recommendations shall be considered binding conditions-of-approval, 
subject to any modifications herein;  
7. The applicant's final revised plans shall be signed and sealed by a professional engineer;  
8. The Notice-of Decision to be issued by the Wetlands Agent shall be included on the final 
revised plans, and all conditions-of-approval shall be listed and incorporated into those plans. 
The final revised plans shall be subject to review and approval by the Wetlands Agent or by 
the Chair of the Commission;  
9. Either repair alternative depicted by the applicant on the submitted plan is acceptable. Prior to 
the onset of the project the applicant shall confirm in writing which option has been chosen 
and the reason(s) for the choice. 
 
2. IWC #26-1276 
2623 Dixwell Avenue 
Pardee Brook Diversion Channel 
Maintenance activities—removal of sediment and brush 
Applicant: Town of Hamden 
Hamden Engineering Department staff engineer Steve Mcallister presented the application to 
the Commission. He gave a brief history of the channel, which he said was constructed as part of 
a flood control strategy after heavy flooding impacted the area of the Meadowbrook Co-op. 
Maintenance activities had last been conducted in 2012, he said. The current application seeks to 
remove sediment and cut back brush in order to improve water flow through the channel.  
Mr. Mcallister reported that the amount of sediment to be removed is similar to the amount 
that was removed in 2012. He also mentioned that the previous approval limited work to three 
feet vertical height above the stream channel floor, and said a similar limit could be appropriate 
for the current proposal. Mr. Mcallister agreed to all other conditions recommended by Mr. 
V ocelli as well. He concluded his presentation and welcomed questions from the Commission. 
Commissioner Shadle recalled the public comment made at the start of the meeting and asked 
if this project related to the concerns raised by Mr. Vece. Mr. Mcallister believed Mr. Vece had 
been referring to Pardee Brook, which he distinguished from the Pardee Brook Diversion 
Channel; the work being proposed at this time addresses the diversion channel. Mr. White 
explained that the channel is designed to reroute water flow from Pardee Brook around the 
Meadowbrook Co-op and into Shepard Brook. The Engineering and Public Works Departments 
have been evaluating the area to improve flood prevention measures, he said, and proper 
maintenance of the diversion channel would be a quick and simple start.  
Commissioner McCollum asked how often the diversion channel is mowed. Mr. Mcallister 
replied that it was routinely mowed two to three times per year. Commissioner McCollum then 
inquired about leaving a strip of vegetation along each channel bank. Mr. Mcallister confirmed
Page 6 of 8 Inland Wetlands Commission 10.7.26 Minutes 
 
that was the intention, and that the three-foot vertical height limit for clearing would keep 
vegetation in-tact at the top of each slope. 
Commissioner McCollum asked how much of the flow from Pardee Brook gets diverted via 
the channel. Mr. Mcallister could not provide specific figures but said the majority of the water 
goes to the diversion channel. Mr. White offered additional details for the overall stormwater 
system in the Meadowbrook area. He said that proper maintenance of the diversion channel was 
the first step in a longer process to address the flooding issues the community has faced. When 
asked how the sediment and brush materials would be removed, Mr. Mcallister replied that a 
backhoe would most likely be used. 
Chairman Milazzo granted Mr. Vece permission to address the applicant. Mr. Vece expressed 
his frustration at the perceived lack of action regarding the Meadowbrook community’s concerns. 
He was under the impression that the current proposal would address Pardee Brook and the health 
and safety issues the community feels it poses, and asked when they might expect something to 
be done. Mr. White assured him that the diversion channel maintenance was part of a larger plan 
to improve conditions in the area.  
There were no further questions or comments from members. Commissioner Schneider 
moved to approve the application, pending discussion of the conditions recommended by 
Mr. Vocelli. Commissioner Hayes seconded the motion. Mr. V ocelli then read his 
recommended conditions into the record, as follow: 
1. The Town shall conduct sediment and brush removal operations whenever warranted or 
dictated by field conditions. Mowing of the project work area in order to facilitate proper 
access & egress shall continue to be allowed; 
2. If temporary stockpiles or transfer areas prove to be necessary, the location of same shall be 
depicted on the final revised plans. Any stockpile(s) shall be secured with appropriate erosion 
controls, and said controls shall be checked on a weekly basis until the material is properly 
dispersed; 
3. A downstream turbidity curtain and oil containment boom shall be installed prior to the onset 
of any brush or sediment removal operations; 
4. The uprooting of vegetation shall be avoided, and root systems shall remain in place; 
5. Removed sediment and brush shall ultimately be dispersed in a suitable upland area at least 
100 feet from any wetland or watercourse; 
6. The October 2, 2026 Regional Water Authority comment letter shall be included on the final 
revised plans. RWA recommendations shall be considered binding conditions-of-approval, 
subject to any modifications herein;  
7. Removal operations shall generally be conducted during dry weather periods, unless an 
excessive build-up of sediment dictates otherwise; 
8. The applicant's final revised plans shall be signed and sealed by a professional engineer;
Page 7 of 8 Inland Wetlands Commission 10.7.26 Minutes 
 
9. The Notice-of Decision to be issued by the Wetlands Agent shall be included on the final 
revised plans, and all conditions-of-approval shall be listed and incorporated into those plans. 
The final revised plans shall be subject to review and approval by the Wetlands Agent or by 
the Chair of the Commission. 
Commissioner McCollum wondered if the comments from the RWA should be incorporated 
as conditions of approval. Mr. Vocelli pointed out that an existing condition stated that “RWA 
recommendations shall be considered binding conditions-of-approval,” which satisfied 
Commissioner McCollum. 
Commissioner Schneider asked Mr. Vocelli if Condition 1 was intended to create an open-
ended permit to the Town to perform maintenance of the channel. Mr. Vocelli confirmed it would 
allow the Town to perform the requested work as needed for the duration of the permit, which he 
said would be five years with the right to renew for five more. Work beyond that timeline would 
require a new permit. 
Commissioner Shadle suggested the addition of a condition that requires the Town to assess 
the functionality of the channel after the work has been performed. The Commission discussed 
the benefit of evaluating the effectiveness of the channel at serving its stated flood prevention 
purpose. However, Mr. Livshits clarified that it was an existing diversion channel and the current 
request was for maintenance activity. He said that evaluating the effectiveness of the original 
design might be going beyond the Commission’s purview. Commissioner Schneider inquired 
whether the channel had performed effectively when it was first constructed, which Mr. White 
confirmed. Commissioner Schneider declined to incorporate the suggested condition into his 
motion.  
With no further questions, comments, or suggestions, Chairman Milazzo called for a vote. 
Commissioners McCollum, Stone, Schneider, Shadle, and Laliberte voted in favor of 
approving IWC #26-1276; Commissioner Hayes voted against. The application was 
approved subject to the conditions recommended by Mr. Vocelli. 
 
 C. Old Business/New Business 
 
 
 
1. Review of September 2, 2026, Regular Meeting minutes 
   Chairman Milazzo called for any corrections or edits. Commissioner Schneider moved to 
approve the minutes as written. Commissioner McCollum seconded the motion. All 
members voted in favor; the September 2, 2026, meeting minutes were approved as written.  
 
2. Review site inspection schedule 
 Mr. V ocelli reported that there were no pending site inspections to schedule.
Page 8 of 8 Inland Wetlands Commission 10.7.26 Minutes 
 
3. Storm water catch-basin medallion update 
 Mr. V ocelli said he had been informed by Ron Walters, a retired RWA Senior Environmental 
Analyst who has continued to be involved in the medallion project, that all of the necessary 
contracts have been signed. He added that the Hamden Land Conservation Trust is working to 
organize a team of volunteers to complete the installation.  
 
D. Adjournment 
 
 
 
 
 
      
 Chairman Milazzo called for a motion to adjourn. Commissioner McCollum made the 
motion, seconded by Commissioner Hayes. All were in favor and the Chairman adjourned the 
meeting at 8:32p.m.  
 
 
 Submitted By: ______________________________ 
Maisie Albis, Commission Clerk
